name: Self-Debugging with Execution Feedback
org: Google DeepMind, University of California, Berkeley
one_liner: Iterative program synthesis loop driven by unit-test execution traces, compiler diagnostics, and line-by-line rubber-duck code explanation.

loop.proposes: A code LLM synthesizes a candidate program (Python, C++, or SQL) and generates a line-by-line behavioral explanation.
loop.judged_by: The language runtime and unit-test suite execute the candidate program and return exact assertion failures, stack traces, or syntax errors.
loop.steers: Execution error messages paired with the behavioral trace condition the next repair iteration until all tests pass.

headline_result: Improved pass@1 by up to 12 percentage points across TransCoder C++-to-Python translation, Spider text-to-SQL, and MBPP Python synthesis.
caveat: Correctness is bounded by the unit-test suite available during the debugging loop.
beyond_harness_note: Deterministic compiler and unit-test execution traces gate termination and steer iterative code repair.
algorithmic_authority: Interpreter runtime and unit-test execution oracle

sources.title: Teaching Large Language Models to Self-Debug (ICLR 2024 / arXiv:2304.05128)

verification.notes: Checked against Chen et al., ICLR 2024.
